answer: A Sybil swarm fails at the enrollment anchor: every identity must present a hardware-signed quote from one physical chip, pinned in the ledger, so a thousand virtual keys collapse into a single admitted seat. Admission also posts a bond, a slab of shale any challenger can expose and slash. Reputation accrues only along attested slots, so a voyage of fake accounts costs one chip plus one forfeitable bond each, a price that scales linearly while influence stays capped, killing the margin that makes Sybil attacks pay.
